title: Target firms: entry programs, timelines and stated requirements (WO-036)
method: Collected 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 through a web search index restricted to each firm's own domains (firm careers pages and the firm's own job postings), plus the press for published applicant counts. The build environment could not open the pages themselves (every firm site, dol.gov and bls.gov were unreachable from it), so each statement is the search index's extract of the cited page, kept close to its words. checked_at is the date of that search, not a page fetch. Nothing here was written from memory.
known_limits: Postings change every cycle: a requirement here is what the cited page said when it was indexed. Several indexed postings were more than a year old; their statements are kept only where the page is the firm's own and the program still runs.
Requirements are the ones a page states. A page that states none gives none here; nothing is filled in from general knowledge.
Base rates are only the firm's own published applicant counts (as reported by the press). A third-party estimate is never a base rate. Most firms publish none.

No firm here publishes who it hired (schools, majors, prior jobs). That population needs a licensed dataset (Revelio Labs, People Data Labs or Coresignal), which is the owner's spend decision. Until then the answer says so in one line and never describes hired candidates.

hired_candidate_data.needs: A licensed hiring dataset (Revelio Labs, People Data Labs or Coresignal). Owner's spend decision; not bought as of 2026-10-20.
